title: Forest fire consumes thousands of acres and destroys homes
seoTitle: Forest fire consumes thousands of acres and destroys homes
subtitle: Authorities confirm dozens of houses destroyed and issue evacuation orders
excerpt: The rapid spread of a massive forest fire forces mass evacuations and destroys dozens of homes in the area.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A massive forest fire is consuming more than 15,000 acres in the Peavine Mountain area and forcing thousands of residents to leave their homes. Fire‑fighting crews have achieved 27% containment, while local authorities confirm severe material damage and dozens of homes destroyed.

The fire’s advance and evacuation orders

The blaze started and spread quickly across the area, creating scenes of dense smoke, ash, and flames near properties. Residents reported the sky turning reddish as the flames raced up the mountain. About 90,000 people faced evacuation orders, and tens of thousands remain under orders to either leave immediately or stay on high alert.

Fire‑fighting efforts

Firefighters have managed to contain part of the affected area and are using helicopters, containment lines, and retardants to protect dense vegetation zones and flat terrain. Teams are also working around a natural‑gas pipeline in the affected zone. The mountainous terrain, continuous fuels, and critically dry conditions continue to challenge suppression efforts.

Damage assessment and investigations

Authorities confirm that dozens of houses have been destroyed and others damaged, with assessments still ongoing. Search and rescue teams are sweeping the area with the help of dogs. The governor has declared a state of emergency to mobilize resources, and the investigation points to human activity as the cause of the fire.

Guidance for residents

Officials reiterate the request for the public to avoid the affected region and not return to burned areas due to lingering hazards. Traffic routes are reopening gradually, but access to certain streets remains restricted. Police advise using emergency numbers only for immediate threats to life or property.

Information from KRXI2, KSNV.
